title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a smooth complex-analytic curve. P_X is the sheaf of local étale (locally biholomorphic) maps X → P^1(C), i.e. local projective coordinates.

The quantity G. For two such coordinates t and s, the previous page defines
G(t,s) = (−2 s'''/s' + 3 (s''/s')^2) dt^2, with derivatives taken with respect to t.
This equals −2·S_t(s)·dt^2, where S_t(s) is the Schwarzian derivative of s with respect to t, so G(t,s) is a holomorphic quadratic differential.

What the previous page established.
- (1) Invariance in the second variable under affine maps and under s ↦ 1/s. Hence G extends to étale maps to P^1 and is invariant under Möbius maps acting on s.
- (2) The cocycle identity G(t,s) + G(s,r) = G(t,r). This is the chain rule for the Schwarzian, S_t(r) = S_s(r)(ds/dt)^2 + S_t(s).
- (3) Compatibility with restriction to open sets.

This page derives formal consequences.
- Putting s = t in (2) gives G(t,t) = 0.
- Putting r = t then gives antisymmetry, G(t,s) = −G(s,t).
- From these, invariance in the first variable follows: G(gt, s) = G(gt, t) + G(t, s) = −G(t, gt) + G(t,s) = G(t,s), since G(t, gt) = G(t,t) = 0.
- This yields (1 bis) and (4): G is invariant under PGL_2(C) acting on either argument.

Axiomatic packaging. Let H = Aut P^1(C) ≅ PGL(1,C) = PGL_2(C), the invertible 2×2 matrices modulo scalars. Grothendieck records a morphism of sheaves G : P_X × P_X → ω_X^{⊗2} with two properties:
- (I) G is H×H-invariant;
- (II) G satisfies the additive cocycle (Chasles) relation.

He then announces that ODE theory gives a converse (III, on the next page):
- (a) on connected U, G(t,s) = 0 implies s = g·t for some g in H;
- (b) for fixed t, the map s ↦ G(t,s) induces an isomorphism H\P_X ≅ ω_X^{⊗2}. Surjectivity holds because locally any quadratic differential is a Schwarzian: take the ratio of two independent solutions of y'' + (q/2)y = 0 (up to normalisation).

Where this leads. The next page formalises this as an ω^{⊗2}-torsor Conn_X, the sheaf of projective connections. It comes with an H-invariant map c : P_X → Conn_X such that G(t,s) = c_s − c_t, an isomorphism H\P_X ≅ Conn_X, and functoriality under étale maps.

Purpose. This is preparatory material for second-order linear ODEs and projective structures on curves, in a dossier on Gauss–Manin connections, Picard–Fuchs equations and the Cartier operator. It is presumably aimed at hypergeometric/uniformization examples and a possible char-p analogue.
errors: Minor: H is described as matrices 'mod. matrices diagonales'. It should be modulo scalar matrices; the text reads 'GP(1,C)', presumably meaning PGL(1,C) = PGL_2(C).
Normalisation: G = −2·(Schwarzian) rather than the standard Schwarzian. This is harmless, but signs and constants must be tracked when comparing with the literature.
The derivation of G(t,t) = 0 is stated as 'faisant t=t'' in (2); logically one sets s = t (or r = s) in (2). This is probably a transcription or handwriting issue.
Stating I) and II) as 'conditions' is slightly redundant: invariance in the first variable follows from invariance in the second plus II), as the page itself shows.

ideas.what: Schwarzian derivative as a quadratic-differential-valued 1-cocycle on local coordinates, invariant under PGL_2 on both sides, with G(t,t)=0 and antisymmetry deduced formally from the cocycle identity
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian cocycle / chain rule for the Schwarzian
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Kummer; cocycle viewpoint in Gunning, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces 1966; Hawley–Schiffer 1966)

ideas.what: Sheaf P_X of étale maps to P^1 with PGL_2 action, and a classifying map H\P_X → ω^{⊗2} (relative to a fixed coordinate)
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf of local projective structures; quadratic differentials parametrise projective structures relative to a reference

ideas.what: Converse via ODE theory: zero Schwarzian implies Möbius equivalence; every quadratic differential is locally a Schwarzian
ideas.modern_name: Solvability of the Schwarzian equation via ratios of solutions of a second-order linear ODE

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, careful but entirely classical treatment of the Schwarzian cocycle and its PGL_2 invariances, preparing the standard torsor of projective connections. This was well documented by Gunning and others around the same time and is now the standard (sl_2-oper) picture. Nothing on this page goes beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'GP(1,C)' is presumably PGL(1,C); 'mod. matrices diagonales' should be read as scalar matrices.
In the margin, the crossed-out passage concerns prolonging G(t,s) to the case where both s and t are étale maps X → P^1(C).
